resources.string:
AtlayaSwitch works best with three separate GrapheneOS profiles:

• Owner – the system profile (User 0). Device management, developer options and Shizuku run here; only visible in this profile.

• Private – your everyday profile for daily work, with all the apps and accounts you normally need.

• Away – a deliberately empty decoy profile containing only unremarkable, harmless apps (e.g. camera, maps, an empty browser). It acts as a distraction: anyone taking a quick look at the device (a check, theft, coercion) only sees the mundane, with nothing pointing to further profiles or sensitive data.

This separation is the core of the duress concept: in an emergency, AtlayaSwitch immediately and quietly switches from the active profile to the harmless "Away" profile – no password prompt, no visible menu.

WARNING: AtlayaSwitch is installed in the target profile \"%1$s\" itself. The target profile is meant to stay unremarkable (even to third parties, e.g. during a check) – having AtlayaSwitch installed there reveals that a hidden switching mechanism exists. Please remove it.
Removal failed – please check manually: Settings → Apps → AtlayaSwitch → uninstall in profile \"%1$s\".
Switches to the target profile; the previous profile stays active and unlocked in the background.

After switching, also fully ends the previous profile (its apps are closed, GrapheneOS removes its encryption keys from RAM/hardware registers – the profile goes back \"at rest\") – default. Note: when switching from the \"Owner\" profile, Android may refuse this, since the system user can never be stopped – in that case it silently just switches, with no error message.

Shizuku is not installed – the profile switch won\'t work without it. Best installed from the Play Store; then tap \"Open Shizuku\" here and set up \"Start via Wireless debugging\" once (runs entirely on the device, no PC needed).
Shizuku is not installed. Developer options and Wireless debugging are only visible in the \"Owner\" profile – install and set it up there first, it will then be detected here automatically.
Shizuku is installed but not running (e.g. after a device restart) – required for the profile switch. Please open it here and tap \"Start via Wireless debugging\" once.

Shizuku isn\'t running and can\'t be started from here: Developer options/Wireless debugging are only visible in the \"Owner\" profile. Open it there and tap \"Start via Wireless debugging\" once – it will then keep running system-wide, including here.

Replaces the earlier NFC trigger: tapping a tile in the Quick Settings panel triggers the same switch as the app icon tap – even from the lock screen, without opening the app. Unlike the app icon tap, the tile is visible in the pulled-down panel (icon/name kept deliberately neutral). Add the tile in the panel yourself via the pencil/edit icon afterwards.
